How exactly are renewable storage methods non-scalable? The way I see it there are three situations possible here. The least interesting of course, is no excess energy generation. Here there is no storage issue, no problem. With excess generation there are three sets of circumstances. First, where you have excess generation and your long-term storage capacity is sufficient for even your largest surplus generation. When the grid isn't meeting demand, the storage kicks on and meets it. Next, you have excess generation, your long-term storage is exceeded by your largest excess, but your storage will last long enough to satisfy grid demand until your renewables are at peak generation again (and thus, replenishing the storage). Finally, you have excess generation, but your long-term storage capacity is exceeded by your largest excess, and that long-term storage will not be enough to meet demand during the off-peak hours of your renewable generation. In this case, you build more long-term storage until your energy regime is the first or second situation.

Which of these situations reflects the nonscalability of renewable energy?
